name: Crisil Ltd
title: Crisil Ltd - 500092 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Crisil Q1 FY26 revenue jumped 30.1% and PAT 45.9%, but management flagged FX gains and a USD4.5m timing pull-forward in RAS, so underlying growth is weaker than headline and no numeric guidance was given.

summary.headline: Crisil Q1 FY26 revenue rose 30.1% YoY, helped by a timing-driven USD4.5 million renewal pull-forward and INR14.4 crore FX gain.
summary.overview: Crisil reported strong Q1 FY26 numbers, with revenue up 30.1% YoY, PBT up 35.7% and PAT up 45.9%, though management flagged that a USD4.5 million accelerated renewal closure and a INR14.4 crore FX gain flattered the quarter. Research, Analytics and Solutions (RAS) segment income rose 34.9% to INR735.6 crore with margin expansion to 22.7%, aided by a full quarter of PriceMetrix. Ratings grew about 20.2% YoY on surveillance fees and new ratings, while management said bond issuance fell 12% YoY in Q1 CY26 amid West Asia-driven yield hardening. Management declined to give forward guidance, citing company policy.

segments.name: Ratings (Crisil Ratings)
segments.commentary: Segment revenue grew about 20.2% YoY in Q1 CY26, driven by surveillance fees (linked to prior-year new ratings) and new ratings revenue, plus Global Analytical Centre work delegated by S&P Global Ratings. Bond issuance fell 12% YoY in Q1 CY26 after flattish CY25 growth.

segments.name: Research, Analytics and Solutions (RAS)
segments.commentary: Q1 FY26 income rose 34.9% YoY to INR735.6 crore with segment margin of 22.7% vs 18.3%; includes a full quarter of PriceMetrix (acquired Nov 2025), so not like-for-like. Accelerated renewals at Coalition Greenwich added about USD4.5 million in Q1, which management expects to normalise over the year.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give quantitative guidance; it declined to comment on forward-looking growth rates for GAC, RAS or ratings.
Q1 FY26 revenue and profit are flattered by timing; management expects RAS seasonality to normalise over the rest of FY26 as renewals are pulled forward.
Crisil's India GDP base case is 7.1% for FY26 (6.8% if West Asia conflict extends through April); FY27 CPI projected at 4.5% (up to 4.7%).
Bank credit growth expected at around 13% in FY27 (Crisil Ratings view); bank credit grew 14.5% YoY as of Feb 2026.
Corporate profitability expected to be flat in FY26 and decline about 100 bps in FY27 (Crisil Intelligence view).
capex_capacity: PriceMetrix (Toronto-based wealth analytics) acquisition completed; consolidated from 7 November 2025 and expands wealth management capability.
Canada added as a new geography; company serves 11,400-plus clients in 40 countries with 5,000-plus professionals.
No capex or capacity figures were disclosed in the call.
Company continues to add headcount across technology, Gen-AI and client development, evenly spread across businesses.
Small stake taken in an Indian SME platform company; inorganic evaluation ongoing in core, adjacent and client-segment spaces.
demand_pricing: Global CIB revenue pools rose in 2025 on sales and trading, equities, fixed income and primary capital markets; management saw no decline in client engagement in Q1 CY26 despite West Asia volatility.

Global Analytical Centre growth from new engagements and higher surveillance delegation from S&P Global Ratings; works on a transfer-pricing fixed margin on cost, which management says is similar to the ratings work margin.

Ratings: bond market softness after yields hardened in H2 CY25; bank loans substituting bonds; 10-year G-sec near 7% in March 2026; management says pricing is disciplined but gave no 5-year price-increase figure.

Management said discretionary spend at global banks remains a key monitorable, with only slower decision-making and no cancellations seen; diversification into wealth, private markets and regional banks.
Competition: management said GCCs are an opportunity for Integral IQ, as they need COE set-up and regulatory support.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving consistently high ratings revenue growth (16-17%) versus weak bond and credit indicators?
qa_highlights.answer: Subodh Rai said surveillance revenue is driven by strong new ratings in 2024-2025, plus investor preference for best-in-class ratings and IRF growth; he cautioned that one quarter may not be indicative and pricing is handled deal by deal with discipline.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a discretionary spend slowdown at global banks and any Gen-AI deflation risk in financial services?
qa_highlights.answer: Amish Mehta said client engagement is intact, with only slower decision-making and no cancellations; Dinesh Venkatasubramanian said AI is seen as more opportunity than risk and is being used across functions.

qa_highlights.question: How did the accelerated renewals affect the next quarters in RAS?
qa_highlights.answer: Dinesh Venkatasubramanian said contracts normally closed in later quarters were closed in Q1, which will smooth seasonality in subsequent quarters; he gave no quantified impact beyond the USD4.5 million.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue, PAT and EBITDA of PriceMetrix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined, saying it discloses only RAS and Ratings segment numbers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rate of GAC growth and the S&P fixed margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose the fixed margin or forward growth, saying it is benchmarked on transfer pricing and that it does not comment on forward-looking statements.

risks_watch: Q1 FY26 flattered by USD4.5 million renewal timing and INR14.4 crore FX gain; watch normalisation of RAS in Q2-Q3.
West Asia conflict could delay decisions and capex, slow bond and loan borrowing, and weaken the IPO pipeline.
Bond-market softness and bank-loan substitution: yields near 7% and a rate hike would hurt bond issuance.
Gen-AI: risk from faster model improvement and slower client adoption; INR appreciation against USD would hurt margins despite hedging.
Discretionary spend at large global investment banks remains the key monitorable.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and margins across businesses, but cautious on the outlook: management would not give forward guidance and deferred on rating growth, pricing, GAC margins and PriceMetrix numbers. It repeatedly urged investors to judge annual rather than quarterly performance.
key_quotes: And I think that is something that is not being seen as we speak right now.
This is largely a timing effect, and we expect this to normalize over the course of the rest of the year.
So, I would say opportunity is about being able to demonstrate value for the work that we do.

growth.why: Management declined to give company-level forward guidance citing policy; Q1 growth of 30.1% was flattered by a ~USD4.5m renewal pull-forward, a INR14.4 crore FX gain and a PriceMetrix acquisition, with no capacity additions or capex disclosed, so the outlook is unclear.
